body:
## SUMMARY

Fix Linux CPU_ONLY static-library consumers failing to link with duplicate
CoordinateManager definitions. Exclude the legacy coordinate_manager.cpp when
the unified coordinate_manager.cu is compiled as C++; keep the unified CPU
implementation and its out-of-line destructor. CUDA source selection is unchanged.

The new CPU change is a five-line build fix against upstream main `f4ac612`,
plus a configured-target regression test. Fix commit `21774d4`; test `66d087a`.
Current head `4ac4292` also merges the existing PR #32 allocator-namespace
compatibility prerequisite for CUDA 12.4, preserving that PR's ancestry rather
than recreating its fix. Review/merge PR #32 before this stacked update.

## TECHNICAL DETAILS

The CPU source glob collects the legacy.cpp, while MINK_DUAL_BACKEND_SOURCES
also contributes coordinate_manager.cu with LANGUAGE CXX. Both define the
constructor and nine other manager methods. A consumer requiring both archive
members gets duplicate definitions from GNU ld. The unified implementation owns
the destructor and remaining manager functionality, so retaining that source is
necessary.

The fix removes exactly the legacy path from MINK_CPU_SOURCES in CPU_ONLY.
The new CTest reads SOURCES from the actual configured minkowski_cpp target and
requires exactly one unified implementation and no legacy implementation.
It does not reconstruct the glob logic in a second implementation.

## TESTING

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Before: Linux pinned-image baseline41507998304 | Three repeated CPU_ONLY builds fail at core_tests link with duplicate CoordinateManager symbols; no tests executed |
| After: Linux source rebuild41511100024 | All three library/consumer builds pass; CTest13/13 passes in each |
| Independent full native integrationa67f671 | CPU full build and CTest14/14 pass; actual build.ninja contains only the unified coordinate manager object |
| Standalone upstream-based branch configuration | Pass; CMake4.2.3/MSVC19.44 with existing CPU LibTorch2.15 |
| Registered cmake_cpu_coordinate_manager_sources | 1/1 passed on actual configured library target |
| Adversarial source-list fixtures | Correct target passes; legacy duplicate, repeated unified and missing unified inputs all fail as expected |

The Linux after-run's overall CI status is failed: a later, unrelated standalone
adaptive sanitizer compile incorrectly requested C++17 for a C++20 defaulted
operator. The complete library rebuild and all13 CTest suites had already passed.
This limitation is preserved, not described as a green CI run. Corrected harness
[CI 41514149790](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790)
now passes all three jobs: modified-source rebuild, CTest 14/14 and standalone
split ASan/UBSan 6/6 with zero findings. Pre/post binary identities, source
manifests, rebuilt linkage, JUnit and actual Linux RSS were independently audited.

The initial upstream PR CI also exposed main's existing CUDA 12.4 allocator
namespace failure in bench_adaptive_kmap.cpp. It is exactly the defect already
fixed by PR #32; merge `4ac4292` incorporates that existing prerequisite. The
original failed check remains in history and the new exact-head CI is separate.

Linux logs and source/binary identities:
[baseline failure](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41507998304),
[rebuilt library and13-suite runtime](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41511100024),
[corrected complete container validation](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790).
These inherited matrix labels are repetitions of one pinned image in CPU_ONLY;
they are not three CUDA runtime-version validations.

## BENCHMARKS

This fixes a link failure and makes no numerical or runtime-performance claim.
Before/after source selection is two competing definitions versus one canonical
implementation. Build wall time is not compared: the surrounding research
integration targets/source sets changed and the original build did not complete.

| Requested metric | Before | After | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Link correctness | Duplicate-symbol failure | Library and all13 suites link/run | Functional improvement |
| Runtime latency/throughput | Unavailable for failing consumer | Not separately benchmarked | No speedup claimed |
| CPU/GPU peak memory | Not a comparable completed workload | Not separately measured for this source-selection fix | No memory improvement claimed |
| Kernel duration | Not applicable | Not applicable | No kernel or arithmetic change |
| Percentage performance improvement | Not applicable | Not applicable | A failed link has no meaningful runtime ratio |

## MACHINE LEARNING RESULTS

Not applicable to this build-only fix. The container's four-method ML smoke
suite passed as part of the13-suite regression run; no accuracy gain is claimed.

## TRADEOFFS

The legacy source remains in the repository; it is excluded only from CPU_ONLY
library target selection. Removing it entirely would be a separate cleanup.
The regression test requires MINK_BUILD_TESTS and CPU_ONLY. Native Windows
validation and Linux container execution are reported separately. Container GPU
execution was unavailable; the change does not alter the non-CPU_ONLY branch.

## REPRODUCTION

Use the existing image without installing a host development environment:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src:ro" -v mink-cpu-link-build:/build \
  acaicia/minkowski4cpp@sha256:a4bf4c4e91ef5f4e50089f435005ca07f1a0a48deeeb9814ca4b526974de79ba \
  bash -lc 'cmake -S /src -B /build -GNinja -DCPU_ONLY=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/libtorch -DMINK_BUILD_TESTS=ON && cmake --build /build --parallel 2 && ctest --test-dir /build --output-on-failure'
```

Use a fresh build volume per revision. Upstream baseline `f4ac612`, CPU fix/test
candidate `66d087a`, current dependency-complete head `4ac4292`.
The standalone configuration/source-selection test can run immediately after
configuration with `ctest --test-dir /build -R cmake_cpu_coordinate_manager_sources -V`.
The original upstream revision has no registered source-selection guard.

The container runs Ubuntu24.04/GCC13.3.0, CMake4.2.3, LibTorch2.15.0 and
CUDA13.4/nvcc13.4.92 dependencies in CPU_ONLY mode. Native configuration used
Windows11, Ryzen5 5600X6C/12T,16GiBRAM, MSVC19.44, CPU LibTorch2.15.0.
The broader native integration also has RTX2080SUPER8GiB/SM75 and driver610.88;
that GPU is not used by this configured CPU source-selection test.


### Completed current-head upstream compilation

Current PR head `4ac4292e40fd78c4d3b81cdc3e775898737647f8` passes all three production build profiles in
[the upstream CI run](https://github.com/QuiteLiterallyConnor/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41517260319). Actual logged combinations are CUDA12.4.131 /
LibTorch2.5.1, CUDA13.2.78 / LibTorch2.15.0, and CUDA13.4.92 / LibTorch2.15.0.
Independent log inspection verified the expected head ancestry in the checked-out
synthetic PR merge, CPU_ONLY=OFF, CUDA object compilation and installation.
This is compilation coverage, separate from the passed14-suite CPU container
execution and native CPU/CUDA tests. No container GPU runtime claim is made.

body:
## SUMMARY

Add a reproducible ModelNet10 input path to the four-representation classification
harness, prevent summaries from mixing different datasets with identical sample
counts, and report Linux process peak RSS with explicit memory scopes. The
existing procedural dataset remains the default. Include a three-seed real-object
pilot and checksummed raw evidence, with the model/input differences disclosed.

## TECHNICAL DETAILS

- Standard-library Python preprocessing reads meshes directly from the official
  ZIP, preserves original train/test membership, selects deterministic per-class
  subsets and samples triangle surfaces proportional to area. It stores bounding
  box normalization, source/split hashes and every selected object identity.
- A LibTorch-independent C++ reader validates fixed local filenames, binary
  headers/sizes, checksums, per-class histograms, finite bounded coordinates and
  unique nonoverlapping sample IDs before conversion to tensors.
- `--dataset-dir` supplies point/sample counts and data seed; conflicting CLI data
  options are rejected. Generated procedural examples remain unchanged.
- Summary aggregation compares the complete dataset identity and manifest across
  runs. Historical unidentified procedural cohorts remain readable but cannot
  mix with explicitly identified datasets. It validates before printing a table
  or replacing an existing CSV.
- A dependency-free helper preserves Windows PeakWorkingSetSize and adds Linux
  `getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss` with KiB-to-MiB conversion, with Darwin's
  byte units handled separately. Unsupported/failing APIs return -1. Output
  identifies lifetime RSS and training-loop-plus-epoch-evaluation CUDA peaks.
- Correct Gaussian documentation to describe the existing adaptive bridge and
  its frozen geometry and marginal-axis covariance approximation.

Dataset feature `0e5c4fe`, summary guard `7460c7e`, RSS helper `2ceceea`.
The measured pilot runtime is separately identified as combined integration
`0a4b62a83a98b091497e996773c68b6f89c38a3c`. Documentation/reporting changes
are not represented as another set of model training results.

## TESTING

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Standalone C++ dataset loader | 22 cases passed; header/size/hash/label/bounds/path/split regressions |
| Python preprocessing | 5 tests passed; deterministic sampling, area weighting, malformed/degenerate OFF, archive split/binary roundtrip |
| Summary CLI guards | 20 tests passed; mismatched manifests, malformed data, duplicate identities, incomplete curves, invalid metrics and cohort mismatch |
| Portable RSS allocation test on Windows | Passed; touched 64 MiB and observed 4.40625->68.4219 MiB; peak stayed 68.4219 MiB after release |
| Focused native CTest at RSS source 2ceceea | 4/4 passed (loader, RSS, summary, preprocessing) |
| Measured integration 0a4b62a full native CTest | CPU 11/11 and CUDA 11/11 passed |
| Completed ML trials | 12/12 passed: 4 methods x 3 seeds x 6 epochs |
| Independent metric/provenance audits | Both passed; every confusion/P/R/F1 and training-time sum recomputed |
| Raw evidence SHA256 verification | All 46 files and 12 expected trial identities passed |
| Modified-source Docker execution | Three jobs passed 14/14 suites, actual Linux RSS unit/high-water checks, and split ASan/UBSan: [run41514149790](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790) |

The summary bug has a before/after reproduction using the same counts, seeds,
epochs and learning rate with one training-split SHA256 changed: the baseline
accepts the incompatible pair; the new summary rejects it before output.

Exact focused checks:

```sh
cmake --build /build --parallel 2 --target point_dataset_tests benchmark_memory_tests
ctest --test-dir /build -R 'point_dataset_tests|benchmark_memory_tests|ml_summary_tests|modelnet_preprocessing_tests' --output-on-failure
python benchmarks/modelnet10_results/verify.py
python benchmarks/ml_representations_summary.py benchmarks/modelnet10_results/raw --seeds 1,2,3
```

## BENCHMARKS

This change extends experiment coverage and measurement correctness. It does not
claim a library latency or memory optimization. External ModelNet input could not
be loaded by the previous harness. Linux RSS previously returned unavailable;
actual Linux helper execution passed in all three audited container jobs. Kernel execution
time is not isolated by this ML harness. CPU inference/model benchmarking was
not performed; CPU execution was exercised by the correctness suites.

The following is a practical systems comparison under the same input subset and
training budget, not a before/after speedup caused by this PR. Means and sample
standard deviations are over three seeds; MiB values are rounded. Exact raw
allocator values, reserved peaks, latency ranges and all memory records are in
`benchmarks/modelnet10_results/raw/`.

| Method | Train seconds | Cached batch1 latency ms | Batched evaluation samples/s | Peak allocated VRAM MiB | Peak reserved VRAM MiB | Lifetime RSS MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| uniform |12.0+/-2.8|37.36+/-5.13|446+/-40|57|76|3777+/-24|
| adaptive |6.7+/-0.4|10.86+/-0.36|948+/-11|171|200|4078+/-13|
| gaussian |2.6+/-0.2|2.31+/-0.12|6738+/-225|42|58|3771+/-0|
| adaptive_gaussian |5.8+/-0.3|11.85+/-1.66|1135+/-74|94|120|3949+/-1|

Adaptive active elements are 368.89 versus 785.81 for uniform (-53.1%), while its
training-loop allocated VRAM is roughly 3x greater. This is evidence that active
voxel count alone is insufficient to infer practical memory savings.

Median conversion times are 0.22+/-0.04, 0.98+/-0.23, 6.07+/-0.17 and 5.93+/-0.64 ms
per object respectively. Conversion is excluded from cached inference/throughput;
the two median distributions must not be summed and called measured end-to-end
latency. Whole pipeline inference and separate memory scopes remain future work.

## MACHINE LEARNING RESULTS

The subset has 400 training/200 test objects, 1024 points/object, 40/20 objects per
class. Every method uses six epochs, batch 16, Adam learning rate 0.001, fixed
data seed 2026 and initialization/shuffle seeds 1,2,3. Original split membership
and no-augmentation preprocessing are preserved. Full six-epoch convergence,
per-class metrics and confusion matrices are included in the evidence.

| Method | Accuracy% | Macro precision% | Macro recall% | Macro F1% | Parameters | Input channels |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|uniform|74.5+/-2.8|76.1+/-2.4|74.5+/-2.8|74.3+/-2.9|677930|2|
|adaptive|78.0+/-1.7|80.2+/-1.2|78.0+/-1.7|77.6+/-1.7|882650|3|
|gaussian|79.5+/-2.6|82.3+/-1.2|79.5+/-2.6|78.4+/-3.5|110218|11|
|adaptive_gaussian|80.8+/-1.3|82.2+/-1.5|80.8+/-1.3|80.6+/-1.0|885242|9|

The combined method observes +6.3 percentage points versus uniform. The models
have different architectures, parameter counts and feature information; this
does not isolate representation quality or establish statistical superiority.
The Gaussian set MLP receives means/normals/scales/counts, while sparse conv
models receive different occupancy/density/level or bridge-aggregated features.
The report includes the complete feature definitions. There was no validation
split or hyperparameter selection; introduce one before further tuning.

## TRADEOFFS

- These are small, contended pilot measurements on a shared Build PC, sampled
  CPU utilization 23.8%-81.9%, with unrelated GPU use. Within each seed method
  order was fixed, so this is not a balanced quiet-machine timing comparison.
- CUDA atomics remain nondeterministic. Seeds freeze data, sample ordering and
  initialization without promising bitwise cross-run/toolkit identity.
- Conversion runs on the host and is substantial for both Gaussian modes. The
  mixture drops cells with fewer than three points. Those preprocessing choices
  can affect both accuracy and cost.
- Peak RSS is a process-lifetime high-water mark. CUDA's existing `*_train`
  fields include per-epoch evaluation; separate phase peaks remain unmeasured.
- Full manifests contain source hashes and identities, but no redistributed CAD
  meshes or points. Same-ID/exact-hash split checks do not detect near duplicates.
- Loader identity uses FNV-1a for portable corruption detection, not adversarial
  authentication; recorded SHA256 provenance provides the stronger audit identity.
- Darwin unit conversion is implemented but has no macOS execution result.
- Docker on standard GitHub Linux runners is CPU-only. Native CUDA results do
  not imply GPU container execution or three-toolkit compatibility.
- This extends the existing bridge/ML harness PRs #26/#31 and compatibility PR #32.
  The branch includes the independent CPU manager fix and configured-target guard
  from PR #54 via merge d46eea3; its final focused CTest passed 5/5.

## REPRODUCTION

Hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6C/12T, 16 GiB RAM, RTX 2080 SUPER 8 GiB, driver 610.88.
Native toolchain: Windows 11, MSVC 19.44, CUDA 13.4.3, LibTorch 2.15.0, Release.
Measured source 0a4b62a, executable SHA256
`ec62ba12f3e29c4b4c23f53c0bbd51296c2e77e805d970c69f990eeef0c6c095`.
Dataset archive SHA256
`9d8679435fc07d1d26f13009878db164a7aa8ea5e7ea3c8880e42794b7307d51`.
Processed manifest SHA256
`983109bf609859eccc4ae302e1ae966fb6a5537032d6f8c139022779f5f36e6c`.
Full split hashes, source IDs and exact per-process CLI arguments are preserved.

Reuse the existing image:
`acaicia/minkowski4cpp@sha256:a4bf4c4e91ef5f4e50089f435005ca07f1a0a48deeeb9814ca4b526974de79ba`.
The internal container harness rebuilds modified source and verifies source
manifest, CMake dependency/archive linkage and executable hashes; it rejects the
preinstalled Minkowski library. Its completed run URL, source identity, commands and JUnit are recorded below.

```sh
python benchmarks/prepare_modelnet10.py --archive /data/ModelNet10.zip --download \
  --output /data/subset40-20-p1024-s2026 --train-per-class 40 --test-per-class 20 \
  --points 1024 --seed 2026
cmake --build /build --parallel 2 --target ml_representations point_dataset_tests
CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 \
  /build/ml_representations --method uniform --dataset-dir /data/subset40-20-p1024-s2026 \
  --device cuda --epochs 6 --seed 1 --batch 16 --kmap-part-reuse-mb 512 \
  --fused-apply 1 --deterministic 0 --output /results/uniform-seed1.json
```

The cache/fusion options reproduce the measured integration runtime; they are
absent from the standalone dataset feature's earlier base. Repeat all four modes
and seeds 1,2,3 in fresh processes, preserving logs and without overlapping GPU
benchmarks. `benchmarks/modelnet10_results/README.md` explains every timing scope,
feature definition, limitation and source/result identity in detail.


### Executed container validation and reproduction

Docker CPU execution is now verified by [corrected run 41514149790](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790),
source `aa74d97`. All three repeated jobs rebuilt the library from modified
source in `acaicia/minkowski4cpp@sha256:a4bf4c4e91ef5f4e50089f435005ca07f1a0a48deeeb9814ca4b526974de79ba`, passed all 14 CTest suites, and passed six standalone
adaptive split cases under GCC ASan/UBSan with zero findings. Source manifests,
CMake/archive linkage, pre/post binary hashes and JUnit were independently
audited. The installed Minkowski archive was rejected. All three labels use
the same CPU_ONLY image; no three-toolkit or container GPU execution is claimed.

The earlier baseline run41507998304 failed to link duplicate CPU manager symbols.
Runs 41511100024 and 41512323659 rebuilt successfully and passed 13/13 and 14/14
suites respectively in all three jobs, then failed a standalone sanitizer command
that incorrectly used C++17 for a C++20 type. Those failures and successful test
stages remain preserved; the corrected run fixes the flag and executes the
sanitizer first. Documentation workflow successes are excluded from validation.

To repeat the actual CPU container path using the frozen source:

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP.git test/docker-runtime
git worktree add ../mink-container-validation aa74d97
docker build --progress=plain --build-arg JOBS=2 \
  -f ../mink-container-validation/docker/Dockerfile ../mink-container-validation
```

The runner recorded four logical CPUs and approximately 15.6 GiB RAM; CPU model
was not recorded and is not inferred. Image tools: GCC 13.3.0, CMake 4.2.3,
LibTorch 2.15.0+cu134 and CUDA 13.4 dependencies. GPU work below is native
supplementary evidence, not execution by this CPU_ONLY container.

The combined native integration `a67f671` independently passed CPU 14/14
and CUDA 14/14 using LAZY loading, including 117 CUDA Gaussian cases. Later
evidence/test-registration head `e5bf8d0` has an identical engine tree; its new
checks passed CPU 2/2 and CUDA 1/1. An initial EAGER run timed out the existing
SSIM 17x300 reference at 420.288 seconds while about 125 MiB GPU memory was free.
The same binaries passed the complete LAZY retry in 116.41 seconds, with no
filtering, rebuild, tolerance change or timeout increase. The failed run remains
preserved; its cause was not isolated and EAGER stress behavior is not qualified.

Actual Linux 64 MiB touched-allocation results: 2.938->66.938 MiB; 3.047->67.047 MiB; 3.047->67.047 MiB. Each peak remained
nondecreasing after release. Lifetime RSS is not a resettable phase counter.


### Completed current-head upstream compilation

Current PR head `d46eea3e23890e46da7c9b77a42a14f287620aed` passes all three production build profiles in
[the upstream CI run](https://github.com/QuiteLiterallyConnor/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41517409288). Actual logged combinations are CUDA12.4.131 /
LibTorch2.5.1, CUDA13.2.78 / LibTorch2.15.0, and CUDA13.4.92 / LibTorch2.15.0.
Independent log inspection verified the expected head ancestry in the checked-out
synthetic PR merge, CPU_ONLY=OFF, CUDA object compilation and installation.
This is compilation coverage, separate from the passed14-suite CPU container
execution and native CPU/CUDA tests. No container GPU runtime claim is made.

title: test: add ModelNet10 datasets and audited representation experiments

body:
## SUMMARY

Distribute the Gaussian rasterizer's ten warp-reduced backward attributes across
ten lanes, so they issue adjacent atomic additions together. This reduces
isolated synthetic backward-kernel latency by 3.18% to 29.27% on an RTX 2080
SUPER. Representative real-scene training remains approximately flat; this PR
does not claim a training, accuracy or memory improvement.

This change stacks on Gaussian gather PR #53 (`229f04d`). Measured runtime is
`b96db27aa5ef68e67d8c8bc3b3e6fa3a7548dcac`; its direct-raster benchmark parent
is `dbead49`. Later documentation commits do not change measured runtime.

The full CPU_ONLY container integration also includes the independent CPU
source-selection fix from PR #54. Linux static consumers of CoordinateManager
need that prerequisite; native branch suites and combined-container results are
reported separately below.

## TECHNICAL DETAILS

The prior kernel reduces all ten attributes using the same shuffle-down tree,
then lane zero executes ten scalar atomic instructions. The changed kernel keeps
that reduction tree, broadcasts each lane-zero result, and assigns attribute k
to lane k. Lanes zero through nine issue one warp instruction to adjacent
attributes. Zero sums remain suppressed. Full-mask shuffles remain warp-uniform,
including image edges and inactive pixels. Current-stream launches, shared
Gaussian IDs, forward math, projection, tile construction and public APIs are
unchanged. Floating-point accumulation across warps remains nondeterministic.

The original path remains available through the internal
`cuda_raster_backward_parallel_atomics()` comparison switch, default enabled,
and benchmark `--parallel-atomics 0|1`. This process-wide switch is for controlled
tests; changing it concurrently with application launches is unsupported.

Static inspection of the measured object shows 62 to 58 registers, 55 to 65
shuffle instructions and 10 to 1 global atomic-add instructions. Both versions
use 11,268 shared bytes and no stack/local spills. These are static binary
properties, not measured dynamic occupancy or hardware-counter results.

## TESTING

Added three registered Gaussian tests covering 0/1/31/255/256/257/513
contributions per tile, partial 19 by 35 image edges, nonuniform RGB/depth/alpha
loss, a nondefault CUDA stream, exactly zero upstream gradients and ten
finite-difference checks. Serial/parallel gradient tolerance is 2e-5 relative
plus 2e-6 absolute; finite differences allow 1% relative plus 0.002 absolute.
Observed differences remained below 9.54e-7 across focused and sanitizer runs.

| Validation | Result |
|---|---|
| Full CPU CTest | 4/4 suites passed; adaptive 119 passed/1 CUDA skip, Gaussian 47 passed/8 CUDA skips |
| Full CUDA CTest | 4/4 suites passed; adaptive 123/0, Gaussian 71/0 |
| Adaptive versus uniform smoke / framework | Passed in both builds; nine framework cases each |
| Added focused tests | 3/3 passed, including all ten finite differences |
| Compute Sanitizer memcheck | 3/3 tests; zero errors |
| Compute Sanitizer racecheck | 3/3 tests; zero hazards, errors or warnings |
| Compute Sanitizer initcheck | 3/3 tests; zero errors |
| Independent evidence audits | All 80 A/B processes, source/input/binary identities, raw invariants and final native receipts passed |
| Docker CPU runtime | Three repeated jobs passed 14/14 suites and split ASan/UBSan; source aa74d97, [run41514149790](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790) |

No sanitizer exclusions were used. Raw logs, JUnit, SHA256 manifests, static CUDA
review and interrupted-experiment history are in
`benchmarks/gaussian_parallel_atomics_results/`.

## BENCHMARKS

Ten paired process rounds reverse serial/parallel order each round. There are
80 successful processes. Synthetic workloads use 32 by 32 tiles, 256 Gaussians
per tile, five warmups and 30 CUDA-event samples per process. Real-scene runs use
139,410 Gaussians at 512 and 1024 pixels, three warmups and ten synchronized
wall-time samples per process. Tables show medians of process medians; complete
min/max ranges and paired changes are retained in the raw summary.

| Workload / metric | Serial ms | Parallel ms | Change | Parallel lower |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Row groups / isolated GPU backward kernel | 2.02486 | 1.43217 | -29.27% | 10/10 |
| Sparse / isolated GPU backward kernel | 2.36523 | 2.10533 | -10.99% | 9/10 |
| Dense / isolated GPU backward kernel | 9.89513 | 9.58031 | -3.18% | 8/10 |
| Real 512 / backward wall latency | 14.48255 | 14.17745 | -2.11% | 5/10 |
| Real 1024 / backward wall latency | 26.89975 | 26.69355 | -0.77% | 7/10 |
| Real 512 / training step | 27.39870 | 27.37945 | -0.07% | 6/10 |
| Real 1024 / training step | 66.58185 | 67.08795 | +0.76% | 6/10 |

| Derived phase throughput | Serial /s | Parallel /s | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Row-group isolated kernel launches | 493.86 | 698.24 | +41.38% |
| Sparse isolated kernel launches | 422.79 | 474.98 | +12.34% |
| Dense isolated kernel launches | 101.06 | 104.38 | +3.29% |
| Real 512 training steps | 36.50 | 36.52 | +0.07% |
| Real 1024 training steps | 15.02 | 14.91 | -0.75% |

Throughput is the reciprocal of the corresponding latency, not a separate
measurement. Synthetic kernel throughput excludes other rendering and training.

| Memory metric (MiB) | Serial | Parallel | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 render backward CUDA allocated peak | 196.5239 | 196.5239 | 0% |
| 1024 render backward CUDA allocated peak | 232.8652 | 232.8652 | 0% |
| 512 render CUDA reserved peak | 244 | 244 | 0% |
| 1024 render CUDA reserved peak | 308 | 308 | 0% |
| 512 complete-process working-set peak | 965.1914 | 965.1309 | -0.006% |
| 1024 complete-process working-set peak | 976.2812 | 976.2207 | -0.006% |

Render forward allocated peaks also match exactly (100.1484/129.7222 MiB).
Working-set differences are noise. Training-phase VRAM and real-scene
kernel-only duration were not collected; no corresponding improvement is claimed.

## MACHINE LEARNING RESULTS

Not applicable to this kernel-only change. The real-scene harness measures a
rendering/training step, not convergence, reconstruction quality or trained model
accuracy. No model accuracy or convergence claim is made.

## TRADEOFFS

The workstation was contended: observed CPU load ranged roughly 38% to 94%,
and background GPU memory use was about 6.8 GiB. Unchanged forward-path aggregate
medians moved +3.28% at 512 and +2.70% at 1024. Small real-scene differences,
including the 1024 training regression, are reported without asserting a
performance change beyond noise. Initial severe outliers remain in the report.
Only the tested RTX 2080 SUPER architecture is covered.

The initial run stopped after 60 successful processes because Windows rejected a
receipt-file write while a reader held it. The failure receipt and output hashes
are preserved. Identity-checked resume ran the missing 20 processes only, after
another experiment released the shared lock. It did not overwrite earlier
results. The writer now atomically replaces receipts with bounded retries.

The preceding per-warp bounds experiment (`8438c04`) was rejected: dense kernel
+4.95%, row groups +2.40%, real 512 backward +4.11% with zero of ten lower pairs.
Its source and results remain preserved in the separate negative-experiment
record. No part of that rejected optimization is in this candidate.

## REPRODUCTION

Native supplementary hardware/software: Ryzen 5 5600X, six cores/twelve threads,
16 GiB system RAM; RTX 2080 SUPER 8 GiB, sm_75, driver 610.88; Windows 11,
MSVC 19.44, CUDA 13.4.3, LibTorch 2.15.0 cu134, Release. Use the repository's
existing pinned Docker image for dependency setup; completed runtime evidence is
recorded in the executed container section below. Native CUDA execution is
separate from Docker CPU validation; no container GPU execution is claimed.

Build the measured checkout with CUDA and Gaussian benchmarks enabled, then run:

```sh
cmake --build build --parallel 2 --target gaussian_raster_backward_bench gaussian_render_bench gaussian_tests adaptive_tests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --timeout 420
build/gaussian_tests gaussian_parallel_atomics
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 99 build/gaussian_tests gaussian_parallel_atomics
compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck --error-exitcode 99 build/gaussian_tests gaussian_parallel_atomics
compute-sanitizer --tool initcheck --error-exitcode 99 build/gaussian_tests gaussian_parallel_atomics
build/gaussian_raster_backward_bench --pattern row-groups --tiles 32 --per-tile 256 --warmup 5 --iterations 30 --parallel-atomics 0 --output row-groups-serial.json
build/gaussian_raster_backward_bench --pattern row-groups --tiles 32 --per-tile 256 --warmup 5 --iterations 30 --parallel-atomics 1 --output row-groups-parallel.json
build/gaussian_render_bench --input tests/data/test.ply --counts 0 --sizes 512,1024 --devices cuda --warmup 3 --iterations 10 --train --parallel-atomics 0 --output render-serial.json
build/gaussian_render_bench --input tests/data/test.ply --counts 0 --sizes 512,1024 --devices cuda --warmup 3 --iterations 10 --train --parallel-atomics 1 --output render-parallel.json
```

Repeat ten times with reversed order each round, using fresh output names, no
overlapping compiles/GPU workloads, and the same scene SHA256 recorded in the
receipt. Repeat synthetic runs for `dense` and `sparse`. The exact original
PowerShell launch/build/test commands, source and executable hashes, data hash,
raw samples, summaries and reproduction scripts are in the evidence directory.
Run `python verify_evidence.py` inside that directory to verify every frozen
file and independently recompute aggregate and paired summary metrics.

Future work: profile real-scene kernel share and stalls on an isolated GPU,
then evaluate additional GPU architectures before generalizing these findings.


### Executed container validation and reproduction

Docker CPU execution is now verified by [corrected run 41514149790](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790),
source `aa74d97`. All three repeated jobs rebuilt the library from modified
source in `acaicia/minkowski4cpp@sha256:a4bf4c4e91ef5f4e50089f435005ca07f1a0a48deeeb9814ca4b526974de79ba`, passed all 14 CTest suites, and passed six standalone
adaptive split cases under GCC ASan/UBSan with zero findings. Source manifests,
CMake/archive linkage, pre/post binary hashes and JUnit were independently
audited. The installed Minkowski archive was rejected. All three labels use
the same CPU_ONLY image; no three-toolkit or container GPU execution is claimed.

The earlier baseline run41507998304 failed to link duplicate CPU manager symbols.
Runs 41511100024 and 41512323659 rebuilt successfully and passed 13/13 and 14/14
suites respectively in all three jobs, then failed a standalone sanitizer command
that incorrectly used C++17 for a C++20 type. Those failures and successful test
stages remain preserved; the corrected run fixes the flag and executes the
sanitizer first. Documentation workflow successes are excluded from validation.

To repeat the actual CPU container path using the frozen source:

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP.git test/docker-runtime
git worktree add ../mink-container-validation aa74d97
docker build --progress=plain --build-arg JOBS=2 \
  -f ../mink-container-validation/docker/Dockerfile ../mink-container-validation
```

The runner recorded four logical CPUs and approximately 15.6 GiB RAM; CPU model
was not recorded and is not inferred. Image tools: GCC 13.3.0, CMake 4.2.3,
LibTorch 2.15.0+cu134 and CUDA 13.4 dependencies. GPU work below is native
supplementary evidence, not execution by this CPU_ONLY container.

The combined native integration `a67f671` independently passed CPU 14/14
and CUDA 14/14 using LAZY loading, including 117 CUDA Gaussian cases. Later
evidence/test-registration head `e5bf8d0` has an identical engine tree; its new
checks passed CPU 2/2 and CUDA 1/1. An initial EAGER run timed out the existing
SSIM 17x300 reference at 420.288 seconds while about 125 MiB GPU memory was free.
The same binaries passed the complete LAZY retry in 116.41 seconds, with no
filtering, rebuild, tolerance change or timeout increase. The failed run remains
preserved; its cause was not isolated and EAGER stress behavior is not qualified.

### Exploratory uncertainty and publication supplement

Whole-pair bootstrap intervals (20,000 draws) are row-groups [-30.74,-26.56]%,
sparse [-17.39,-7.00]% and dense [-6.51,+0.19]%. The dense3.18% point estimate is
inconclusive. Real training intervals also cross zero:512px [-3.59,+4.09]%,
1024px [-4.94,+4.03]%. Small cohorts, serial load and uncertain pair independence
limit these intervals. Descriptive sign-test p values are unadjusted and address
paired-win probability rather than the ratio-of-medians estimand. Nothing is
confirmatory, and original point estimates/raw outputs remain unchanged.

Metadata-only commit348e6b8 adds94 JSON/log/manifest files initially omitted by
ignore rules. Every one of the203 evidence SHA256 identities and the manifest
now matches committed Git blobs. The engine code remains byte-identical to
the tested runtime; this correction adds no new timing claim. The
[supplement and independent review](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/tree/11b0d679d7edf719fc889483646dc3f8c5439c75/benchmarks/round10)
and all package verifiers also pass from a fresh Git export.


### Completed current-head upstream compilation

Current PR head `348e6b83da8bb068274ac02288f01defdbeaf5a3` passes all three production build profiles in
[the upstream CI run](https://github.com/QuiteLiterallyConnor/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41519874048). Actual logged combinations are CUDA12.4.131 /
LibTorch2.5.1, CUDA13.2.78 / LibTorch2.15.0, and CUDA13.4.92 / LibTorch2.15.0.
Independent log inspection verified the expected head ancestry in the checked-out
synthetic PR merge, CPU_ONLY=OFF, CUDA object compilation and installation.
This is compilation coverage, separate from the passed14-suite CPU container
execution and native CPU/CUDA tests. No container GPU runtime claim is made.

title: perf(gaussian): parallelize reduced raster gradient atomics

body:
## SUMMARY

Compact repeated occupied x cells before splitting adaptive cached parts, then
assign leaves with monotonic cursors within each sorted level. This reduces
repeated CPU sorting and boundary searches in the existing opt-in part cache.
This PR stacks on #52; the split-only diff starts at `647450b`.

The full CPU_ONLY container integration also includes the independent CPU
source-selection fix from PR #54. Linux static consumers of CoordinateManager
need that prerequisite; native branch suites and combined-container results are
reported separately below.

## TECHNICAL DETAILS

Runtime candidate: `95093e2938e939ad5dd954c33ae4ea583879fa4d`; original
runtime `2623c56`, baseline documentation head `647450b`. Public APIs, canonical
leaf order, part boundaries, weights and mathematical reductions are unchanged.
Six independent old/new differential tests include 250 deterministic randomized
cases. The baseline implementation is retained solely in test/benchmark code.
The report explains the O(N + U log U) boundary construction and the cursor
assignment worst-case tradeoff, without claiming a benefit for every layout.

## TESTING

Audited historical native results: CPU CTest 5/5, CUDA CTest 5/5. CPU adaptive:
133 passed/8 skipped; CUDA adaptive: 144 passed/0 skipped. Six split tests passed
in both builds. Gaussian: CPU 36 passed/4 skipped, CUDA 42 passed/0 skipped.
Registered smoke/framework suites passed. CPU skips are CUDA-only coverage.
Exact kernel-map indices, ordering, weights, values and gradients remain covered
by the existing part-cache regression tests. No numerical tolerances changed.

New portable runner contract checks:
`python benchmarks/test_adaptive_part_split_compare.py`: 6/6 passed.
Independent evidence audit reparsed all 108 process logs and recomputed 26
summary rows; source/binary bindings, balanced order, checksums and all recorded
leaf/pair/cache invariants passed. Logs, JUnit and checksummed raw evidence live
in `benchmarks/adaptive_part_split_results/`.

Docker CPU execution is now verified by [corrected run 41514149790](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790),
source `aa74d97`. All three repeated jobs rebuilt the library from modified
source in `acaicia/minkowski4cpp@sha256:a4bf4c4e91ef5f4e50089f435005ca07f1a0a48deeeb9814ca4b526974de79ba`, passed all 14 CTest suites, and passed six standalone
adaptive split cases under GCC ASan/UBSan with zero findings. Source manifests,
CMake/archive linkage, pre/post binary hashes and JUnit were independently
audited. The installed Minkowski archive was rejected. All three labels use
the same CPU_ONLY image; no three-toolkit or container GPU execution is claimed.

## BENCHMARKS

Six balanced interleaved A/B process pairs per workload. CPU phase: 3 warmups,
15 timed repeats/process. Complete batch maps: valid adaptive tensors from 64
ellipsoid samples, 2048 points each, depth 3, batch 16, 4 epochs, 512 MiB host
part cache. CUDA synchronization and EAGER module loading in both arms. Raw
ranges and every memory metric are in the accompanying report.

## MACHINE LEARNING RESULTS

## TRADEOFFS

The shared host had substantial background CPU/GPU load despite exclusive lab
benchmark locks; results are contended paired observations. Cursor scans can

Whole-process peaks do not isolate temporary vector memory. No Gaussian
algorithm or CUDA kernel is changed by this improvement.

## REPRODUCTION

Exact native scripts, commands, hardware, executable SHA256 and source commits

### Executed container validation and reproduction

Docker CPU execution is now verified by [corrected run 41514149790](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41514149790),
source `aa74d97`. All three repeated jobs rebuilt the library from modified
source in `acaicia/minkowski4cpp@sha256:a4bf4c4e91ef5f4e50089f435005ca07f1a0a48deeeb9814ca4b526974de79ba`, passed all 14 CTest suites, and passed six standalone
adaptive split cases under GCC ASan/UBSan with zero findings. Source manifests,
CMake/archive linkage, pre/post binary hashes and JUnit were independently
audited. The installed Minkowski archive was rejected. All three labels use
the same CPU_ONLY image; no three-toolkit or container GPU execution is claimed.

The earlier baseline run41507998304 failed to link duplicate CPU manager symbols.
Runs 41511100024 and 41512323659 rebuilt successfully and passed 13/13 and 14/14
suites respectively in all three jobs, then failed a standalone sanitizer command
that incorrectly used C++17 for a C++20 type. Those failures and successful test
stages remain preserved; the corrected run fixes the flag and executes the
sanitizer first. Documentation workflow successes are excluded from validation.

To repeat the actual CPU container path using the frozen source:

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP.git test/docker-runtime
git worktree add ../mink-container-validation aa74d97
docker build --progress=plain --build-arg JOBS=2 \
  -f ../mink-container-validation/docker/Dockerfile ../mink-container-validation
```

The runner recorded four logical CPUs and approximately 15.6 GiB RAM; CPU model
was not recorded and is not inferred. Image tools: GCC 13.3.0, CMake 4.2.3,
LibTorch 2.15.0+cu134 and CUDA 13.4 dependencies. GPU work below is native
supplementary evidence, not execution by this CPU_ONLY container.

The combined native integration `a67f671` independently passed CPU 14/14
and CUDA 14/14 using LAZY loading, including 117 CUDA Gaussian cases. Later
evidence/test-registration head `e5bf8d0` has an identical engine tree; its new
checks passed CPU 2/2 and CUDA 1/1. An initial EAGER run timed out the existing
SSIM 17x300 reference at 420.288 seconds while about 125 MiB GPU memory was free.
The same binaries passed the complete LAZY retry in 116.41 seconds, with no
filtering, rebuild, tolerance change or timeout increase. The failed run remains
preserved; its cause was not isolated and EAGER stress behavior is not qualified.

### Exploratory uncertainty supplement

Whole-pair bootstrap intervals (20,000 draws) for the CenterSampled warm median
change are CPU [-41.82,-8.02]% and CUDA [-15.85,-9.16]%. VolumeWeighted intervals
cross zero: CPU [-26.33,+3.86]%, CUDA [-21.03,+12.18]%; those point estimates are
inconclusive. Small cohorts, serial load and uncertain pair independence limit
the intervals. Sign tests target paired-win probability, not the same
ratio-of-marginal-medians estimand; p values are unadjusted and exploratory.
Original point estimates and all raw outputs remain unchanged. The
[supplement and independently reviewed code](https://github.com/itsSio/Minkowski4CPP/tree/11b0d679d7edf719fc889483646dc3f8c5439c75/benchmarks/round10)
reproduce from a fresh Git export.


### Completed current-head upstream compilation

Current PR head `b5c4bd8ab8b0f3557f04ff1cca09feea8e95922b` passes all three production build profiles in
[the upstream CI run](https://github.com/QuiteLiterallyConnor/Minkowski4CPP/actions/runs/41517408982). Actual logged combinations are CUDA12.4.131 /
LibTorch2.5.1, CUDA13.2.78 / LibTorch2.15.0, and CUDA13.4.92 / LibTorch2.15.0.
Independent log inspection verified the expected head ancestry in the checked-out
synthetic PR merge, CPU_ONLY=OFF, CUDA object compilation and installation.
This is compilation coverage, separate from the passed14-suite CPU container
execution and native CPU/CUDA tests. No container GPU runtime claim is made.
